transcript:
Acme Healthcare — Discovery Meeting
Date: 2026-10-29
Attendees: Director of Infrastructure (Acme Healthcare), Seller

Director of Infrastructure: Thanks for making the time. As I mentioned on the intro call, our primary storage arrays are reaching end of support in Q2 2027. We need to replace them before that deadline or we risk running unsupported hardware under our HIPAA audit.

Seller: Understood. Can you tell me more about the workloads that depend on those arrays?

Director of Infrastructure: The biggest consumer is our medical imaging archive. We have three hospitals generating DICOM files around the clock. Beyond that, we run our electronic health record system and a few administrative file shares. The imaging workload alone is growing about 20% per year.

Seller: What happens if a storage array goes down during clinical hours?

Director of Infrastructure: That is our biggest concern. We had a partial failure 18 months ago — it lasted about 40 minutes, but it caused real disruption in two of our clinics. We cannot afford that happening again. High availability with no single point of failure is a hard requirement.

Seller: What recovery time objective do you need?

Director of Infrastructure: Four hours. That is what our risk team signed off on. We need full recovery within four hours.

Seller: Are there any data protection or compliance requirements beyond HIPAA?

Director of Infrastructure: Encryption at rest is mandatory for patient data. We also need centralised management because our storage team is only three people. We cannot have a system that requires a specialist for every routine task.

Seller: Have you thought about capacity — do you know how much usable storage you currently have deployed?

Director of Infrastructure: Honestly, I do not have that number ready. We are spread across three sites with older arrays and the capacity reporting is not reliable. I would need to pull that from the array management tools, which I can do before our next call.

Seller: That would be very helpful. What about budget — has a project budget been approved?

Director of Infrastructure: That is where it gets complicated. For capital spend above a certain threshold we need CIO approval. I do not want to name a number today, but I would say we are looking at a meaningful capital investment. The CIO knows about this project at a high level but has not been in any of our calls.

Seller: Would it be useful to include the CIO in the next session, or at least brief them on the options before we go further?

Director of Infrastructure: Probably yes. Let me talk to them first and figure out the best way to bring them in. They are very time-constrained.

Seller: Of course. What timeline are you working to beyond the end-of-support date?

Director of Infrastructure: Ideally we would have new hardware installed and tested by end of Q1 2027 — so roughly March 2027. That gives us a buffer before the support cutoff.

Seller: Are there any concerns about the migration itself — moving data from the old arrays?

Director of Infrastructure: Migration risk is our number one worry after HA. We are a 24-hour operation. We cannot afford extended downtime for a migration. Whatever solution we choose, it needs to support non-disruptive data migration.

Seller: That is clear. Any other concerns I should be aware of?

Director of Infrastructure: Cost. I am not going to pretend budget is not tight. The board is watching every capital spend carefully after last year. I need to be able to justify this investment with a clear business case.

Seller: I understand. As a next step, I would like to propose a technical deep-dive session with your infrastructure team. That will let us map the specific workloads to a proposed architecture. I will send you a summary of what we covered today and a proposed date for the deep-dive — would next week work?

Director of Infrastructure: Yes, next week works. Send me a few options and I will confirm with the team.

Seller: Perfect. I will follow up with a summary and two or three date options by end of business on 2026-10-31.

Director of Infrastructure: Great. I will also have the capacity numbers ready by then.
